h1:
Chiang Mai Night Safari
An Easy Family Tram Ride Through a Night Zoo
intro: Chiang Mai Night Safari is a night zoo where you ride a slow-moving tram through open enclosures — animals roam wide spaces rather than sitting in cages. Many species are more active after dark, so kids get to see giraffes, zebras, rhinos and lions in a very different atmosphere from a daytime zoo. The moment children remember most is when giraffes stretch their necks up to the tram to be fed by hand. It makes for an easy evening out with the family.

blocks.html: Chiang Mai Night Safari sits in Hang Dong district, about 12 kilometres southwest of Chiang Mai city at the foot of Doi Suthep-Pui. It was Thailand's first night safari to use a drive-through tram format instead of walking past caged animals. The tram route runs roughly 5 kilometres and takes about an hour, with a guide sharing facts about each animal along the way. What families enjoy is how close the plant-eating animals come to the tram — kids see them up close without the daytime crowds pressing in around them.
The parts children tend to talk about afterwards are mostly on the tram and around the lake. Here's what to look forward to.

items: Savanna Safari tram zone — an open-grassland zone with over 300 plant-eating animals, including giraffes, zebras, white rhinos, deer and ostriches roaming a wide field.
Feeding giraffes by hand — the highlight kids love most: giraffes lean their necks toward the tram so you can offer them leaves or the feed the park provides.
Predator Prowl tram zone — the meat-eaters' zone with lions, tigers, wolves and crocodiles, viewed from the safety of the tram.
The Jaguar Trail walk — a short walking loop around the lake for early evening, gentle enough for kids to stretch their legs before or after the tram.
Musical fountain and light show — a fountain-and-music display by the lake, a nice pause that younger children enjoy watching.

blocks.title: Tips for bringing kids
blocks.html: Aim for early evening (around 6–7 p.m.), when the night zones open and the air turns cooler. Booking tickets online ahead cuts the queue. Bring a light jacket and mosquito repellent, and if you have a baby or very young child, know that the commentary speakers on the tram are fairly loud — you may want to plan around the noise.

items: Opening hours — open daily. The daytime walking zone (Jaguar Trail) runs from around 11 a.m., while the night tram zones (Savanna + Predator) start around 6 p.m. and run until roughly 10–11 p.m. The ticket office usually closes around 9 p.m.

Approximate fees — pricing differs for Thai and foreign visitors. The safari tram ticket for foreigners is around 1,200 THB, while the Thai rate is much lower; children are about half price, and kids under 100 cm tall and visitors with disabilities enter free. Prices are approximate and can change, so check ticket.chiangmainightsafari.com before you go.

Getting there — about a 20–30 minute taxi, Grab or red-truck (songthaew) ride from Chiang Mai city; if self-driving, drop a pin on "Chiang Mai Night Safari" in Google Maps. Many hotels and tours offer transfers bundled with a ticket.

Suitable ages — it works for all ages and the tram is comfortable even for little ones, but because it's a night activity with loud commentary, kindergarten-age children and up usually get the most out of spotting animals and feeding them.

blocks.title: Safety, value and the animal question
blocks.html: On the tram, keep children seated and arms inside, especially through the predator zone. On value, the part families appreciate most is riding through the open enclosures where animals roam wide spaces — kinder than keeping them in cages. As for the performing-animal shows, the tiger show in particular has drawn animal-welfare criticism over the years and is currently suspended for renovation as of mid-2025. We'd suggest focusing on the safari tram, the open zones and feeding the giraffes — the experiences kids enjoy — and leaving the animal-trick shows to each family's own judgement.

faq.q: What time does Chiang Mai Night Safari open?
faq.a: It's open daily. The daytime Jaguar Trail walking zone opens around 11 a.m., while the night tram zones start around 6 p.m. and run until roughly 10–11 p.m., with the ticket office closing about 9 p.m. Check the park's website for the latest hours before you go.

faq.q: How much is entry to Chiang Mai Night Safari?
faq.a: Pricing differs for Thai and foreign visitors. The safari tram ticket for foreigners is around 1,200 THB, with the Thai rate much lower; children are roughly half price, and kids under 100 cm and visitors with disabilities enter free. Prices are approximate and can change, so check the official website first.

faq.q: Is it suitable for young children?
faq.a: Yes — the tram is comfortable and works for little ones, but it's a night activity and the commentary speakers on board are fairly loud, so plan around the noise if you're bringing a baby. Kindergarten-age children and up usually enjoy spotting animals and feeding the giraffes the most.

The part families appreciate is riding through the open enclosures, where animals roam wide spaces rather than cages. The performing-animal shows — the tiger show in particular — have drawn welfare criticism over the years and are currently suspended for renovation as of mid-2025. We'd suggest focusing on the safari tram and giraffe feeding and skipping the animal-trick shows at your own discretion.

The kids' highlight is feeding giraffes by hand in the Savanna zone. Night tram zones run around 6–10 p.m.; the foreigner tram ticket is around 1,200 THB, less for Thais, half price for children.
